newsitem.title: USA: Florida robbery suspect feels guilty, surrenders.
newsitem.headline: Florida robbery suspect feels guilty, surrenders.

text.p: It was the guilt that got to crack cocaine addict and robbery suspect Tyrie Nelms when he saw his victim on the television news, police said on Thursday.

Nelms, 33, turned himself in on Wednesday after hearing terrified store owner Pong Han's lament on a news show about being robbed twice by the same man, said police in Sanford, Florida, just north of Orlando.

"Never had a bad guy have guilty feelings and come down and turn themselves in. This was a unique one for us," Sanford Police Commander Dennis Whitmire told Reuters. "It sure would be nice if they all had conscience pangs like this."
Nelms told the Orlando Sentinel "it really hit home," when Han, 58, talked of selling or closing up shop.

"Man, I felt so bad, he thought I would shoot him," he said. "I could have easily kicked back and stayed home. I decided to go ahead and face it and take what's coming to me and hope it's not too hard. I ain't regretting it ... yet."

Nelms was released from prison last December after serving 6-1/2 years for the robbery of a jewelry store. He now faces charges in four armed robberies in Sanford during the past two weeks, each of which could land him in prison for life.

He told the Sentinel he was high on crack when he committed the crimes and an accomplice who furnished the gun and getaway car convinced him the robberies were a way of getting money for drugs. "It wasn't me in there," he said. "It was some monster that surfaced out of this habit."
